_exportRoutes_note: Optional. Leave exportRoutes empty and every pulled file type lands under exportRoot, which is the original behaviour. Add routes when different file types belong in different places - raw .job files are datalogger state, while the .csv and scans a surveyor exported are deliverables. 'from' is 'export' (the collector's exportSubPath) or 'root' (the project folder on the device, where Trimble Access keeps .job). Each route gets its own leg in the compare view. Use 'overwrite' collision where filenames must stay exactly as exported - it still never destroys anything, a clash lands as 'name (2).ext' - and note that 'prefix' renames a scan's '<name> Files' folder, which severs the .jxl from its point cloud.

projects.name: Example project
projects._tabletProjectPath_note: Optional. The project's full path on a Windows tablet, when it is named differently there than on the controllers - renaming it on the tablet is not safe, jobs reference their files by path. Goes only into the tablet config written onto the stick. Empty = tabletDataRoot + the controllers' path.
projects._extraDesign_note: Optional. More office folders pushed to the devices, each mirrored into its OWN folder under the project (subPath) - never inside the design folder, whose mirror would delete it. Survey control is the usual one.

exportRoutes._note: The trailing fixed segment (a company folder here) sits under the dated part, so files land in <year>\<month>\OURCO. Duplicate detection still scopes to the whole month, so a file someone later moved into a different company's folder is not pulled again.
exportRoutes.name: QC survey data

exportRoutes._supersede_note: A .job is a live database the crew adds to all day, so a newer copy replaces the backup instead of landing beside it. Without this, every sync of a job still being worked in leaves one more copy. Leave it off (the default) for exported files: two .csv sharing a name are two different surveys and both must be kept.
exportRoutes.name: Job files

exportRoutes._note: Surfaces the surveyor builds on the device. Trimble Access saves them in the project folder beside the jobs, so this reads 'root'. A root route reads only the project folder's own files, never its subfolders, so the .ttm surfaces the office pushed into Design do not come back.
exportRoutes.name: Surfaces

_driveMap_note: Drive letters the tool creates with subst when they are missing, so a fresh login never breaks a sync. S: is the whole team folder, which is what lets every path above be short and identical on every machine. Targets are tried in order and %ENVVAR% is expanded - prefer %OneDriveCommercial% to a C:\Users\<name>\... path, or the config only works for whoever wrote it. A letter that already resolves is never touched.
_autoUpdate_note: A copy running from a git clone fast-forwards itself to the latest main at startup, and restarts on it. Only a clean clone on main is touched. false turns it off.
_tabletDataRoot_note: Optional. The folder that CONTAINS 'Trimble Data' on Windows tablets. Defaults to C:\ProgramData\Trimble, where Trimble Access for Windows keeps it; only set it for tablets set up differently.
_defaults_note: The baseline every collector starts from. Edit it HERE - the GUI deliberately cannot write it, so nobody can turn a one-off tweak into everyone's default by clicking. Reset to defaults (Advanced) puts one collector back on it; collectors already set up keep what they have until you do.

defaults._jobRetentionDays_note: Days of recent work Tidy (run after every Sync, or from its button) must never touch. It only ever removes a job or export whose filename date is older than this AND that is confirmed in OneDrive by name and size - both, or it stays. No date in the name means it is never removed.

_collectors_note: Do not hand-write these. Plug a collector in and press Detect - the serial is read from the USB descriptor (or, for a USB stick, from the volume), the name you give becomes the export filename prefix, and these settings are copied from defaults.

collectors._note: A USB stick as a collector. serial is VOL- plus the volume serial, so it is found wherever Windows mounts it; model is the volume label. exportCollision is 'overwrite' because tablets have already prefixed their exports with their own name; on a stick it wins over each route's collision, so nothing is named twice.
collectors.name: USB-01

collectors._note: A Trimble Connect project as a collector - the one collector written by hand, since Detect cannot find a cloud project. NOT YET TESTED against a live project: Check before the first Sync. serial is any id unique among your collectors. pushOnly: designs go up, nothing comes back. On Connect, prune deletes only design file types the source no longer has and never deletes folders (scans and jobs may exist only there). Sign-in is a browser Trimble ID login; the session is stored DPAPI-encrypted per Windows user, never in this file. The IDs below are placeholders.
collectors.name: Connect
